text: Explain and evaluate the factors which must be considered when deciding whether a claimant has
consented to the risk of harm in tort. [25]
Distinguish between pure economic loss and consequential economic loss in the law of tort and
assess the view that this is an illogical distinction. [25]
Explain the elements of the rule in Rylands v Fletcher and assess the extent to which it can be
categorised as a tort of strict liability. [25]
Section B
Julian, his wife Helen and their four‑year‑old child Oliver are staying in a cabin at the XYZ Holiday
Park. On the first evening, Julian sustains a head injury when he falls on the steep steps up to
the door of the cabin. There is no handrail and the light above the door is not working. There is a
warning sign near the steps but Julian cannot read it in the dark.
The following day, whilst Julian is being treated at the hospital, Helen lets Oliver go to the children’s
play area alone. The climbing frame in the play area is damaged and a sign has been placed on
it stating ‘Danger – Do not use’. As Oliver starts climbing on it, a large section becomes detached
and he falls to the ground, sustaining a broken leg.
Advise the parties as to their rights and responsibilities in this situation. [25]
Dimitri works as a chef in the kitchen of the ABC Hotel. During a busy evening at work, he is
rushing from one part of the kitchen to another when he falls over a box left on the floor by another
staff member and hurts his leg. He is taken to hospital and an X‑ray is taken of his leg. When
Doctor Jones examines the X‑ray, he informs Dimitri that there is no serious injury and sends him
home.
The next day Dimitri is unable to walk and is experiencing severe pain. He returns to the hospital.
A different doctor examines the X‑ray and informs Dimitri that his leg is, in fact, broken.
Advise the parties as to their rights and responsibilities in this situation. [25]
Jared is a college student. He is late for an examination and is running down the corridor at
college. He collides with Eric, knocking him to the ground. Eric is unharmed but very angry. The
next day Eric sees Jared in the college library and approaches him. He tells Jared that he will ‘hurt
him’ once he sees him outside the college. When Jared tries to get away, Eric stands in front of
him blocking his path. Jared pushes Eric out of his way and starts to run. Eric puts out his foot and
trips Jared, who falls and sustains a broken arm.
Advise the parties as to their rights and responsibilities in this situation. [25]
